title: Run the herding part of a dispatch wave in one call
action: Add an additive boolean flag --run to bee dispatch wave (per fb99f277). In prepare.rs run_dispatch_wave, accept the key run in the keys_known list (today: runtime, feature, session-id, limit) and, only when --run is set, hand the finished {wave, skipped, economics} value to a new module verbs/drivers/wave_run.rs (register it in verbs/drivers/mod.rs) instead of emitting it; without --run the output stays byte-identical. Declare the flag on every registry entry that answers to dispatch wave in generated/registry_payload.json (search the file for the string Maximum number of this wave's cells to find the entry and copy the shape of the limit flag), per command-surface R10. wave_run: split the wave items into herding items (tool Bash and payload.command contains `bee herding run`) and native items (everything else, returned unchanged). Run every herding item at the same time, one std::thread each, through the shell resolver in shell.rs, with cwd the main root and payload.stdin piped to the child's stdin; wait for all. Save each child's full stdout to .bee/workers/<cell id>-wave-run.json under the main root. Parse that stdout as the herding run JSON envelope and print one value {ran, native, skipped} where each ran row is {id, exit, outcome, job_id, report_path, head_sha, changed_paths (a count of the envelope's git changed_paths), retryable, envelope_path}, a field missing from the envelope rendered as null (per 39f4fbcf). Exit 0 only when every ran row's outcome is done; print every row on any exit. No retry, no cap, no edit to cells. Keep the spawn behind a function that takes the item list and a runner closure so tests can pass a fake runner. No code comments of any kind (repo rule no_code_comments). Tests, all named with the prefix dispatch_wave_run_: in wave_run.rs a unit test with a fake runner over two herding items (one done, one blocked) asserting the rows, the counts, the saved files and the non-zero exit; in verbs/cells/tests.rs, next to dispatch_wave_returns_a_payload_per_disjoint_ready_cell and reusing wfl4_wave_root and wfl4_dispatch_wave_run, a test that --run over two Agent-tool cells returns both under native, ran empty, and exit success.

truths: bee dispatch wave without --run prints the same bytes as before
bee dispatch wave --run returns one JSON value with ran, native and skipped, where Agent-tool items appear unchanged under native and are never executed
Each herding item runs in parallel and yields one compact ran row while its full envelope is saved under .bee/workers/<cell id>-wave-run.json
The verb exits 0 only when every ran row's outcome is done
